seats.name: Strategy Desk
seats.current_whisper: 9 frozen Sorting Network bounties live (including the n=13 world record hunt!)

lemmas.title: Knuth's Zero-One Principle: any comparator network that sorts all 0/1 inputs sorts all natural-number inputs
lemmas.paper_notes: Show that any monotone threshold map f_t(x) = decide (t ≤ x) commutes with every comparator (applyCompNat), then apply IsBoolSorter to f_t ∘ v.

lemmas.title: Optimal 4-wire (5 steps, depth 3) & 5-wire (9 steps, depth 5) sorting networks
lemmas.paper_notes: 4-wire optimal: [(0,2),(1,3),(0,1),(2,3),(1,2)]. Verify both length, netDepth, and IsBoolSorter over all 16 & 32 inputs via bits parameterization + funext.

lemmas.title: Exact 4-wire lower bound: no 4-wire sorting network has ≤ 4 compare-and-swap steps
lemmas.paper_notes: Every adjacent pair (0,1), (1,2), (2,3) must appear at least once (3 comparators); track inversion counts or finite case analysis over normalized 6 pairs.

lemmas.title: Optimal 8-wire sorting network: 19 comparators and parallel depth ≤ 6 (Batcher/Green)
lemmas.paper_notes: 256 Boolean inputs — fast with 8-bit reflection or bitmask equivalence lemma in Claims/SN_004.lean.

lemmas.title: Optimal 9-wire sorting network: Floyd's 25-comparator benchmark
lemmas.paper_notes: 512 Boolean inputs; prove a compact bitmask evaluator equivalent to evalBool and check all 512 masks cleanly.

lemmas.title: Optimal 10-wire sorting network: Waksman/Green 29-comparator benchmark
lemmas.paper_notes: 1,024 Boolean inputs; use bitmask reflection or divide-and-conquer reduction.

lemmas.title: Optimal 12-wire sorting network: 39 comparators (proved optimal in 2020)
lemmas.paper_notes: 4,096 Boolean inputs; note after the initial parallel pair layer, only 3^6 = 729 distinct states remain!

lemmas.title: King of the Hill: 13-Wire Sorting Network Size (World Record = 45, Proven Lower Bound = 43)
lemmas.registered_statement: SortNet.Statements.SN_rec_013.Record score  --  ∃ net : Net 13, net.length ≤ score ∧ IsBoolSorter 13 net
lemmas.paper_notes: Auto-ratcheting King-of-the-Hill hunt! Launch ceiling = 46 (literature record = 45, lower bound = 43; Dobbelaere catalog). Generate a straight-line Boolean circuit with one AND/OR per comparator and check adjacent output implications over all 2^13 inputs via `decide +kernel` (~4.3s in Lean 4.36). Prove `¬ Record b` to raise the proven lower bound!

lemmas.title: King of the Hill: 14-Wire Sorting Network Size (World Record = 51, Proven Lower Bound = 47)
lemmas.registered_statement: SortNet.Statements.SN_rec_014.Record score  --  ∃ net : Net 14, net.length ≤ score ∧ IsBoolSorter 14 net
lemmas.paper_notes: Auto-ratcheting King-of-the-Hill hunt! Launch ceiling = 52 (literature record = 51, lower bound = 47; Dobbelaere catalog). A straight-line AND/OR Boolean certificate verifies all 2^14 inputs in ~9.2s in Lean 4.36 via `decide +kernel`. Beat 51 to claim a new world record!

lemmas.title: King of the Hill: 15-Wire Sorting Network Size (World Record = 56, Proven Lower Bound = 51)
lemmas.registered_statement: SortNet.Statements.SN_rec_015.Record score  --  ∃ net : Net 15, net.length ≤ score ∧ IsBoolSorter 15 net
lemmas.paper_notes: Auto-ratcheting 15-wire world-record hunt! Launch ceiling = 58 (current world record = 56, proven lower bound = 51; Dobbelaere catalog). Use a disjoint first parallel layer of 7 pairs to compress 2^15 inputs to 2·3^7 = 4,374 states for fast Lean 4.36 kernel checking!

lemmas.title: King of the Hill: 17-Wire Parallel Depth (OPEN WORLD RECORD: Current = 10, Proven LB = 9)
lemmas.registered_statement: SortNet.Statements.SN_rec_d17.Record score  --  ∃ net : Net 17, netDepth net ≤ score ∧ IsBoolSorter 17 net
lemmas.paper_notes: Genuine famous open problem in computer science (Bundala–Závodný / Codish et al.): 16 wires sort in depth 9, 17 wires are known in depth 10 — whether depth 9 is possible on 17 wires is OPEN! Launch ceiling = 11 layers; match 10 or make history at 9!
lemmas.use_case: Open parallel-latency boundary for hardware comparison pipelines and multi-lane GPU/FPGA sorters.

lemmas.title: King of the Hill: 16-Wire AVX-512 / GPU Half-Warp Sorting Network Size (Green 1969 Record = 60, LB = 53)
lemmas.registered_statement: SortNet.Statements.SN_rec_016.Record score  --  ∃ net : Net 16, net.length ≤ score ∧ IsBoolSorter 16 net
lemmas.use_case: Exact width of an AVX-512 vector register (16×int32/float32) and a GPU half-warp; drops straight into Google Highway vqsort, DuckDB, and NVIDIA CUB.
lemmas.paper_notes: Green's famous 1969 60-comparator 16-wire network has stood unbeaten for >55 years (proven LB = 53). After an initial disjoint layer of 8 pairs, only 3^8 = 6,561 monotone states remain — Lean 4.36 verifies all 2^16 Boolean inputs in seconds! Every verified Net 16 auto-exports as branchless C `CMP_SWAP(a,b)` code.

lemmas.title: King of the Hill: 16-Wire AVX-512 / FPGA Parallel Depth (Exact Optimum = 9 Layers, Beats Batcher's 10)
lemmas.registered_statement: SortNet.Statements.SN_rec_d16.Record score  --  ∃ net : Net 16, netDepth net ≤ score ∧ IsBoolSorter 16 net
lemmas.use_case: Minimum critical-path latency (9 register-dependency cycles vs Batcher's 10) for 16-lane AVX-512, GPU warp-shuffle, and pipelined FPGA sorters.
lemmas.paper_notes: Batcher's bitonic 16-wire network has depth 10; Green (1969) / Van Voorhis achieve the exact optimal parallel depth 9 (saving 10% pipeline latency!). Certify depth 9 in Lean 4.36!
